findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an integration test (in 47c8 or 80a5) that creates a ticket then runs a second real create on the same clone, one process no daemon, and asserts the first ticket appears in the second create's similar_tickets
evidence: Parent AC: 'A ticket created on a clone is findable by the next create on that same clone, in one process, with no daemon, background thread, MCP server or CI involved. Checked by: an integration test.'
47c8 AC: 'A ticket created in-process is returned by the next query in that same process...' — actor is 'query', one level below 'create'
80a5 ACs exercise retrieval via injection: 'A create exits 0 with an empty similar_tickets when retrieval returns empty... when retrieval raises' — neither drives a real index
container pairing: parent + 2041-75d6-2a2f-4be9/47c8-97ac-eff3-4e88/80a5-cbb1-ef06-4ba5/b505-d66e-86b3-4446/f10f-c24a-3cfa-449e
findings.finding: Parent AC6 ('A ticket created on a clone is findable by the next create on that same clone, in one process, with no daemon... Checked by: an integration test') is only partially covered. Child 47c8's nearest criterion asserts a ticket is 'returned by the next QUERY in that same process' at the query-API level, not by the next CREATE; child 80a5's surfacing tests inject empty/raising retrieval rather than exercising a live index. No child's integration test asserts an actual create surfacing a prior actual create end to end.
scenarios: An agent creates ticket A, then runs a second create whose text matches A; AC6 requires A to surface, but only the query API (47c8) and injected-retrieval surfacing (80a5) are tested, so a wiring break between create's surfacing step and the live index would pass every child test while failing AC6
findings.suggested_fix: Extend child 80a5 (or 47c8) with an integration-test criterion exercising a real create→create against the live lexical index, asserting the prior ticket surfaces, matching parent AC6's actor and scope.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Assign ownership of the initial corpus embedding-backfill procedure (scheduling/bounding against the shared Bedrock spend cap) to child 2041 or a dedicated child, with an acceptance criterion
evidence: Epic comment: 'the backfill does not trip the spend cap... it is a bounded consumption worth scheduling deliberately (run the one-time backfill on a low-traffic day, or use the vector-raw variant...)' and earlier 'it should be settled in the child's plan before any backfill runs'
2041 Approach describes per-ticket build ('adds the digest-and-embed build step') but has no criterion for the initial corpus backfill or cap scheduling
47c8 builds the lexical index incrementally in-process and takes no embedding/Bedrock cost; f10f only widens the IAM resource list and attests a single real Titan call
container pairing: parent + 2041-75d6-2a2f-4be9/47c8-97ac-eff3-4e88/80a5-cbb1-ef06-4ba5/b505-d66e-86b3-4446/f10f-c24a-3cfa-449e
findings.finding: Owned-by-none scope gap: the initial full-corpus embedding backfill and its interaction with the shared Bedrock daily spend cap is named by the epic as a prerequisite to be settled in the index-and-surfacing child's plan, but no child under this container owns it. Child 2041 owns the per-ticket digest-and-embed build step and is the only Bedrock-calling path, yet neither it, 47c8, nor f10f addresses how the first corpus backfill is run or bounded against the account-wide cap.
scenarios: An operator enabling the embedding tier triggers a first full backfill of ~5,663 tickets' Haiku+Titan calls landing atop the day's existing LLM-Review spend; without an owned plan for scheduling/bounding it, the backfill is run ad hoc
findings.suggested_fix: Add a criterion to child 2041 specifying how the initial corpus backfill is run and bounded (e.g. throttle under the metered ceiling or run the one-time backfill deliberately), or create a sibling that owns it, so the epic-deferred prerequisite has an owner.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State, per failure arm, the disposition the create surfaces using an explicit disposition word: whether a transient embedding failure (throttle/timeout) is retryable (WAIT_AND_RETRY) vs a fatal one (auth/denial), and — for the embedding→lexical chain — which disposition wins when the embedding arm fails so a retryable primary is never masked by the silent lexical degradation.
evidence: 'A create succeeds with an empty or lexical-only advisory when ... the configured embedding provider denies or errors, and when the digest parse yields empty fields.'
'The embedding tier then swaps the ranking function behind an interface' — fallback chain embedding→lexical present
'the empties and retry counters ADR 0122 requires of any consumer' names retry but not the disposition surfaced to the caller
ADR context: 'An installation that cannot reach it configures another model or runs lexical-only' — degradation path, disposition unstated
findings.finding: The plan adds a degradation/fallback chain (embedding tier → lexical tier → empty advisory) but never states the failure-disposition contract per arm: when the embedding provider 'denies or errors', the plan collapses all embedding failures into 'lexical-only advisory' without distinguishing a retryable/transient failure (e.g. a Bedrock 429 throttle) from a fatal/permanent one (e.g. auth denial), and does not state which disposition wins when the embedding arm fails. This is the 1c0d shape — a retryable primary (embedding throttle) can be silently masked by degrading to the lexical tier, with the create reporting success and no retryable signal reaching the caller.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria: 'A create succeeds with an empty or lexical-only advisory when the index is absent, when catch-up fails, when the configured embedding provider denies or errors...'
scenarios: Embedding provider returns a transient 429/throttle: the create degrades to lexical-only and reports success, so a retryable condition is masked and never surfaced as retryable (WAIT_AND_RETRY / exit-11) to the caller.

Embedding provider auth is permanently denied: same lexical-only degradation — correct behavior, but indistinguishable at the advisory level from the retryable case, so no disposition word tells the caller which occurred.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Failure-disposition contract' note to the embedding-tier child: a transient embedding failure (429/timeout) is retryable and must be surfaced as such (e.g. diagnostic marking WAIT_AND_RETRY) even though the create still succeeds with a lexical-only advisory; a fatal failure (auth/denied/digest-empty) is permanent degradation. State that the chain preserves the embedding arm's retryable disposition in the diagnostic rather than collapsing every embedding error into an undifferentiated 'lexical-only' result.

scenarios: An executor implementing the surfacing child must decide whether to emit raw bm25 weights, normalized scores, or cosine similarity, and whether the two tiers must agree on scale

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly whether the lexical-default tier is expected to recover any of the 93 differing-title (semantic) pairs the feature exists to catch, and either add an AC exercising a differing-title case on the default tier or document that semantic recovery is an opt-in-tier-only guarantee so the default's scope is not mistaken for delivering epic 62dc's semantic criteria.

Plan Context: 'the 93 differing-title pairs are what this work exists to catch'

Plan already notes the existing duplicate_create_warning catches the 1,431 same-title pairs; the lexical default's marginal gain over that on the semantic stratum is not established as distinguishable (fts5 vs vector at k=5, p=0.0213 favouring vector)

ABSENCE: no AC requires the DEFAULT-tier configuration to demonstrate recovery of any differing-title (semantic) pair; AC for lexical-only only asserts 'ranked results are returned', not that they catch what the feature exists for
findings.finding: The default (lexical/fts5) tier does not distinguishably beat 'building nothing' on the semantic stratum at k=5 — the exact stratum the plan names as what this work exists to catch — so the out-of-the-box configuration solves a proxy (lexical duplicates, already covered by the existing title-norm journal) rather than the named problem (the 93 differing-title pairs).
findings.location: Approach section, 'Lexical tier, the default' bullet; Acceptance Criteria (no AC asserts the semantic-stratum benefit of the shipped default)
scenarios: An installation runs lexical-only (the default); an agent re-files a differing-title duplicate that only the embedding tier would have surfaced — the feature ships 'available everywhere' but delivers its named value nowhere by default

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the digest retry policy the embedding-tier child must implement — max attempts, the terminal fallback when a retry also fails (empty fields + lexical-only advisory), and whether/where a retry counter increments — and reconcile the plan's 'retry counters ADR 0122 requires' claim with ADR 0122, which mandates only the empties counter.
evidence: Plan: 'the digest step, the configured embedding model, vector ranking, and the empties and retry counters ADR 0122 requires of any consumer'
ADR 0122 Consequences explicitly requires only the empties counter: 'any consumer of this architecture must keep that counter'

ADR 0122 on retry is narrative, not a rule: 'Both succeeded on retry, so the failure is nondeterministic rather than a property of those tickets, and a retry is the correct handling' — no max-attempts, no terminal fallback, no counter semantics defined
measure.py defines the empties counter (lines 592/599-600) but no retry counter exists in the measured code
findings.finding: The plan's embedding-tier child requires 'the empties and retry counters ADR 0122 requires of any consumer,' but ADR 0122 only mandates the empties counter; it narrates retry as 'the correct handling' for the nondeterministic digest-non-answer failure without defining a retry policy or a retry counter (max attempts, terminal behavior if retry also fails, increment placement).
findings.location: Approach / Child decomposition — 'Embedding tier over the pydantic-ai embeddings seam'
scenarios: The embedding-tier executor wires the digest call and must decide how many times to retry a ticket whose digest reply does not answer the task, and what to record when a retry also fails
A reviewer checking the AC 'when the digest parse yields empty fields ... emits a diagnostic' cannot tell whether a non-answering digest should retry-then-empty or empty immediately
findings.suggested_fix: Either amend ADR 0122 to state the retry rule (e.g. 'retry a non-answering digest once; on a second failure record empty fields and increment a retry-exhausted counter') and reference it, or drop the 'retry counters' phrase and define the single-retry-then-empty behavior directly in the embedding-tier child with the counter's increment point named.
